correctness.rationale: Every uncovered wheel rim vertex is adjacent to the vacant hub, so hub survival entails a rim-perfect matching (impossible for odd rims). An even rim has two alternating perfect matchings. Their exact necessary and sufficient independent exponential-clock inequalities integrate to the displayed cyclic m-fold integral. The positive kernel is explicitly trace-class by a rank-one-minus-integrated-rank-one decomposition. Strict positivity isolates one simple spectral-radius eigenvalue, and the eigenfunction equation reduces to a Bessel boundary condition with a unique positive root. Separate exact subset recursion, matching-clock rank integration (rim lengths 4 through 16), and all 8! edge-order enumeration for rim length 4 agree; numerical root is independently checked by a convergent Bessel series. The infinite theorem follows analytically, not by extrapolating finite checks.

value.rationale: Hub avoidance is a geometrically distinguished terminal adsorption event on wheel substrates and is impossible for odd rim size. Even rims have an exponentially rare event, but its exact finite probability is nonlocal in rim clock constraints. The transfer-operator characterization and modified-Bessel decay constant yield a sharp asymptotic across an infinite growing family; the constant is not supplied by a routine substitution into known tree formulas. The fact is a benchmark for rare terminal coverage events on graphs with a diverging-degree adsorption site; it is not a general coverage or mixing theorem.
